title: Investigating psychological and neural correlates of intimate partner violence
summary:
Close relationships offer great potential but also carry the risk of conflicts that can escalate into aggression. A detailed understanding of conflict dynamics leading to aggression and the individual factors influencing cognitive and behavioral processes remains an area of ongoing research. Our study focuses on examining the triggers and dynamics of conflict escalation and blame attribution between romantic partners with differing cognitive control abilities during fMRI scanning.

The primary research questions of this project address three key goals. Goal 1 investigates how cognitive control deficits influence conflict dynamics and aggression in close relationships, specifically identifying the point at which loss of control leads to conflict. Goal 2 examines the neurocognitive patterns underlying conflict emergence in close relationships. Goal 3 explores whether biosignature-specific neural and behavioral patterns exist in the escalation or de-escalation of conflicts.

The long-term aim of this study is to examine neural changes and aggressive interactions in dyads following improvements in cognitive control. To achieve this, we investigate how self-regulation deficits shape conflict behavior in close dyadic relationships by studying dyads consisting of individuals with mental disorders and their romantic partners, as well as dyads consisting of individuals with mental disorders and strangers. Ultimately, the study seeks to identify neurocognitive patterns of conflict escalation and de-escalation and to understand how self-regulation influences aggression and conflict resolution in close relationships.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clear understanding of the study information
- Voluntary signing of the consent form
- Patient group: Individuals with mental disorders according to the DSM-5/ICD-11 criteria, including substance use disorders, psychoses, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, PTSD, ASPD, BPD, CD, ODD, ADHD, ASD
- Romantic partners: In a relationship for at least 6 months
Exclusion criteria:
- Significant cognitive impairments
- Language problems that interfere with understanding the study procedure
- Inability to adhere to the study protocol
- Severe somatic or neurological conditions such as encephalitis, hormonal tumors, or dementia
- MRI-specific exclusion criteria: Claustrophobia and contraindications (e.g., metal implants, Schwangerschaft, etc.)
